posts.caption:
Fake Christmas market booths. Real money gone. Ho ho no.

This month, scammers pretended to be B.C. holiday markets. They sent vendors invitations with real dates, table sizes and prices copied from the markets' own websites. Vendors paid by e-transfer to hold a spot. Some lost more than $1,000.

The same trick works on offices. A "supplier" emails an invoice with new bank details. It looks normal. The money goes to a scammer.

One rule stops both:
New payment details? Call first, using a number you already have. Not the one in the email.

Rushing is the scammer's best friend. A real supplier can wait for a 2-minute phone call.

Save this and share it with whoever pays the bills.

#ScamAlert #BCBusiness #VancouverBusiness #SmallBusinessTips #Cybersecurity

Plot twist: the IT guy calling you isn't your IT guy.

On Oct 28, Canada's Cyber Centre warned that scammers are calling staff at Canadian organizations, pretending to be IT support. They say there's an urgent security update, then send you to a fake sign-in page that looks like your company's. You sign in, they get in.

The fix is easy:
1. Hang up. Politely.
2. Call IT back on a number you already have.
3. Never sign in on a link someone gives you during a call.

Caller ID can be faked, so a familiar number isn't proof. A real IT person won't mind waiting two minutes. A scammer will.

Share this with your team, especially the new person.

#Cybersecurity #ScamAlert #VancouverBusiness #SmallBusinessTips #Microsoft365

Monday morning at the Liontech Zoo. 🦁

“Hi, it’s IT Support! I just need that code we sent you.”

Real IT never asks for your code. Liontech never will.

If someone calls and asks for it:
1. Hang up.
2. Call back on a number you already have.

Which coworker are you: the penguin, the gazelle or the sloth? 🐧🦌🦥

#scamalert #cybersecurity #smallbusiness #vancouverbusiness #manageditservices #officelife

Tuesday at the Liontech Zoo. 🐘

“Hi! It’s your supplier! We have a new bank account. Please pay today.”

New bank details by email? Don’t pay yet. Call the supplier on a number you already have.

Be the elephant. Check before you pay. 🧾

#scamalert #invoicefraud #cybersecurity #smallbusiness #vancouverbusiness #manageditservices

Wednesday at the Liontech Zoo. 🦥

“Updates are ready. Restart now?”
“Remind me… tomorrow.”

47 days later, the raccoon moved in. 🦝

Updates fix the holes scammers use. See an update? Restart today. Not after lunch.

Tag the coworker who’s been clicking “Later” since September. 👇

#cybersecurity #smallbusiness #vancouverbusiness #manageditservices #officelife #updates

Thursday at the Liontech Zoo. 🦒

Email is down. Teams is down. And every client’s phone number is… in email.

Last week’s Microsoft 365 outage lasted about a day. If it happened again tomorrow, how would you reach your team and your clients?

Have a backup list: phone numbers, a group text, a note on your website. Ready before it breaks.

And if “Microsoft Support” calls during an outage asking for your password? Nice try. 🦝

#microsoft365 #outage #smallbusiness #vancouverbusiness #manageditservices #cybersecurity

Friday, 4:59 pm at the Liontech Zoo. 🦝

“It’s your boss. I’m in a meeting. Need 10 gift cards. NOW. Don’t call me.”

Your boss will never text you for gift cards. Call them first.

Has “your boss” ever texted you for gift cards? Tell us below. 👇

#scamalert #giftcardscam #smallbusiness #vancouverbusiness #manageditservices #officelife

Send this to the coworker who orders everything to the office. 📦

A text says your parcel is held and asks for $2.99 to release it. You never ordered a parcel. The fee is the bait; your card number is the prize.

A parcel delivery text you didn’t expect? Don’t pay. Check your orders on the store’s own website.

#blackfriday #deliveryscam #cybersecurity #smallbusiness #vancouverbusiness

Would your office ask a surprise “IT guy” for ID? Tell us below. 👇

Nobody asked ours. That’s how three raccoons in a trench coat got into the server room.

Someone shows up saying they’re from IT support? Ask for ID, then call your IT company to check. And no mystery USB sticks.

#cybersecurity #officesecurity #smallbusiness #vancouverbusiness #officehumor

Send this to the coworker who scans every QR code. ☕

A QR code is just a link, and a fake QR code sticker takes seconds to put up. If it asks you to sign in, stop and check where the link goes first.

There is no free coffee.

#qrcodescam #cybersecurity #blackfriday #smallbusiness #vancouverbusiness

Send this to whoever pays the invoices at your office. 🧾

An email says your supplier changed banks and asks you to pay a new account. Oceanside RCMP reported two B.C. businesses that lost tens of thousands of dollars to emails like that.

New bank details by email? Call the supplier on a number you already have. Then pay.

#invoicefraud #cybersecurity #accountspayable #smallbusiness #vancouverbusiness
